ToolTip.Toolbar.Rescan: Re-run the scan but without enumerating and gathering file informations. Changing certain settings will only take effect during a full scan.
ToolTip.Toolbar.CleanupDb: Removes entries which file no longer exists or which failed on ffmpeg/ffprobe
ToolTip.Filter.Path: Note: if only one item of a group is matching, all group items will be shown
ToolTip.Selection.SymbolLink: Links all selected items to the first unselected item in each group.
ToolTip.Toolbar.MarkNotMatch: Hides this group and exclude it from future scans, except when there is a new duplicate.
ToolTip.Settings.Save: Note: Settings are automatically saved on normal exit
ToolTip.Settings.UseExif: Read creation date from EXIF metadata (DateTimeOriginal) instead of file system date. Useful when file creation date is not accurate.
ToolTip.Settings.GeneratePreviews: Deactivate to save memory by disabling preview images of duplicates
ToolTip.Settings.ExcludeReparse: Symbolic links and junction only. Note this will completely skip these from file enumeration to search.
ToolTip.Settings.ExcludeHardLinks: Unlike reparse points hard links are still included in search but are not considered as duplicates. WARNING: Use this option only when necessary, as it slows down the scanning process considerably!
ToolTip.Settings.ExtendedLogging: If activated ffmpeg and ffprobe errors will be written to the log
ToolTip.Settings.RetrySampling: If activated scan engine will try to generate thumbprints of failed entries each time it is run. Otherwise consecutive attempt will be taken only after cleanup of the database.
ToolTip.Settings.AutoBackup: If activated a backup gets created each time the scan results list gets changed
ToolTip.Settings.NativeFFmpeg: If activated it will call ffmpeg functions natively instead of spawning a new ffmpeg.exe process. This is MUCH(!!) faster. WARNING: You must use the latest SHARED and STABLE ffmpeg version. If something goes wrong then whole VDF will crash.
ToolTip.Settings.IgnoreBlack: Skip black pixels when comparing thumbnails. Lowers the chance for 'false positives' if thumbnails contain too much dark and raises the chance to detect duplicates if one of the thumbnails have black bars and the others not. In rare scenarios this might raise the 'false positives' instead. Slows down the scan speed by a bit.
ToolTip.Settings.IgnoreWhite: Skip white pixels when comparing thumbnails. Lowers the chance for 'false positives' if thumbnails contain too much brightness and raises the chance to detect duplicates if one of the thumbnails have white bars and the others not. In rare scenarios this might raise the 'false positives' instead. Slows down the scan speed by a bit.
ToolTip.Settings.CompareFlipped: Select this option if your video collection might contain horizontally flipped videos and you want them to be detected reliably. Slows down the scan speed by a bit.
ToolTip.Settings.SaveOnExit: If checked you will be asked if you want to save the results when you close VDF
ToolTip.Settings.IncludeNonExisting: If checked non-existing files which have all necessary information are included
ToolTip.Settings.ScanAgainstDb: If checked scan is also performed against your entire database unless database files are excluded otherwise (i.e. exclude list, file path must contain, etc)
ToolTip.Settings.UsePHash: pHash = slower but more robust to re-encoding, resizing, contrast changes etc. Visual similarity = faster, also works on reencoded videos, watermarks etc but less robust. Ignored if you're using an old database with 16x16 graybyte values.
ToolTip.Settings.Percent: Minimum percentage that thumbnails must match before they are considered duplicates
ToolTip.Settings.DurationDiff: Only scan videos against each other where the duration is not bigger/smaller than X %
ToolTip.Settings.Thumbnails: Number of thumbnails generated per file. This only applies to video files. A high number means that the scan takes longer but also the chance of a 'false positive' decreases.
ToolTip.Settings.Parallelism: Limits the amount of concurrent tasks. A value of -1 leaves it up to the system to decide (takes full speed), a value of 1 is most stable (lets you interact with your system while scan runs in background). Maximum should be the amount of physical cores of your CPU.
ToolTip.Settings.CustomFFArgs: FF(mpeg/probe) arguments passed to the end of the internal arguments. Most users can leave this empty.
ToolTip.Settings.CustomCommands: Enter your own commands to open single or multiple files.
ToolTip.Settings.CustomCommandsValue: E.g.: 'nemo --tabs %f', where '%f' is the placeholder for the file(s)
ToolTip.Settings.CustomDbFolder: Specify a custom database folder. Otherwise it uses the current VDF folder.
ToolTip.CustomSelection.IgnoreGroups: While active any group which contain at least one selected item will be ignored
CustomSelection.IgnoreGroups: Ignore groups which contain selected items

ChooseAlgo.Title: Choose Algorithm View
ChooseAlgo.Description: Please choose your graybyte database format. You cannot switch between them later on. The only way is to delete the entire database and start from scratch. Both use visual similarity frame check as default algorithm. In both cases you can find duplicates even if different resolution, added watermark, changes to fps / bitrate etc
ChooseAlgo.16x16Desc:
• Fastest
• More false positives
• pHash algorithm is NOT available
ChooseAlgo.32x32Desc:
• Slower than 16x16 (theoretically 4x slower but practically in most cases +40-60% additional scan time)
• Less false positives
• pHash algorithm is available. More robust when duplicates differ due to changes in contrast, brightness, scaling, or minor edits (but not automatically better, it just works differently)
• When a video is first added to the database, pHash signature is automatically generated, making the initial scan slower. On subsequent rescans, you can switch between both algorithms with negligible performance cost, enabling highly efficient duplicate detection
